claims.head: Nowhere to hide for Rantanen
claims.call: The Blackhawks’ L2 (Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen) spends at least 48% of its 5-on-5 time against the Stars’ first line, against about 33% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Frondell’s line (Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Stars’ first line is Robertson, Hintz and Rantanen.

claims.gist: At home, Jeff Blashill likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Stars’ first line.

claims.head: Who drives the play: the Stars
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Stars have been around the middle of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Stars’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

claims.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
claims.body: On the power play, Dallas is one of the league’s best, but Chicago is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Blackhawks take could cost them.

stakes: The Blackhawks go in eighth in the Central with 6 points, a point behind the Stars, tied for fifth. A regulation win for the Blackhawks would lift them past the Stars.

CHI.head: The Blackhawks face a real test
CHI.body: Even though Chicago has home-ice advantage, Dallas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blackhawks can pull it off if they keep shots to a minimum.

DAL.head: The Stars should have the upper hand
DAL.body: Even though Chicago has home-ice advantage, Dallas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blackhawks’ way back in is keeping shots to a minimum.

items.text: Connor Bedard has a point in seven straight games against Dallas, with a goal in each of the last three.
Wyatt Johnston has missed the Stars’ last two games.
The Stars have been without Matt Duchene all season.
The Blackhawks are newly without Bowen Byram.
